text: Back to the first half. Just how hot were the Spurs?
After one, it was 41 to 22. A road team up 19 after the first quarter of a Finals game? That had never happened. With three minutes left in the second, it was 71 to 42.
say: After one, it was forty-one to twenty-two. A road team up nineteen after the first quarter of a Finals game? That had never happened. With three minutes left in the second, it was seventy-one to forty-two.

text: Vassell went 5 for 5 in the half. Harper, off the bench, 6 of 7. As a team, 14 threes in one half, the most in any Finals half since play-by-play began in 1997.
say: Vassell went five for five in the half. Harper, off the bench, six of seven. As a team, fourteen threes in one half, the most in any Finals half since play-by-play began in nineteen ninety-seven.

text: Playing like that, who wouldn't think this one was over?
But go back and watch those shots one by one, and plenty of them weren't easy looks.

Every NBA arena has a tracking system that puts a make probability on every shot, based on things like shot distance and how hard it's contested. Take two threes: one wide open, one with a defender in your face. The odds aren't even close.
Run the Spurs' first-half shots through that model, and a normal night gets you about 49 points. They actually scored 70. Those extra 21? That's the hot hand.
say: Run the Spurs' first-half shots through that model, and a normal night gets you about forty-nine points. They actually scored seventy. Those extra twenty-one? That's the hot hand.

text: In other words, a big chunk of that 29-point lead came from a hot hand. And a hot hand comes fast, and leaves just as fast. Hold that thought.
say: In other words, a big chunk of that twenty-nine-point lead came from a hot hand. And a hot hand comes fast, and leaves just as fast. Hold that thought.

text: So where did the lead start to slip?
If you ask me, one possession, with 9:27 left in the third.
say: If you ask me, one possession, with nine twenty-seven left in the third.

text: Spurs up 81 to 52, still a 29-point lead, when Wembanyama's elbow catches Karl-Anthony Towns on the chin. After a review, it's a Flagrant 1.
say: Spurs up eighty-one to fifty-two, still a twenty-nine-point lead, when Wembanyama's elbow catches Karl-Anthony Towns on the chin. After a review, it's a Flagrant one.

text: And the problem wasn't just the two free throws. Wemby already had 3 flagrant points in these playoffs. One more, and it's an automatic one-game suspension. In the Finals, who's going to risk that?
say: And the problem wasn't just the two free throws. Wemby already had three flagrant points in these playoffs. One more, and it's an automatic one-game suspension. In the Finals, who's going to risk that?

text: He was asked about it after the game.
And starting with those two free throws, the Knicks went on a 13-0 run.
say: And starting with those two free throws, the Knicks went on a thirteen-nothing run.

text: On the next trip, Keldon Johnson misses three straight putbacks. Anunoby grabs the board and takes off.

Look. The Spurs get four guys back. Three of them each pick up a man, and Wemby sinks to the weak side to protect the rim. But the last man back, Johnson, is a good six feet behind Anunoby. And the whole lane, from the free-throw line to the rim, is empty.
Anunoby cuts right down the middle, Hart hits him in stride, and the closest defender, Wembanyama, is still more than six feet away.
By the time he gets there, Anunoby's already thrown it down!
Then came the threes. Brunson, one. Anunoby, one. Hart, another.
And the Spurs? After Fox's jumper at 9:40, they went six full minutes without a field goal.
say: And the Spurs? After Fox's jumper at nine forty, they went six full minutes without a field goal.

text: After the game, Charles Barkley let them have it on Inside the NBA.
So, was Chuck right?
In the third, the Spurs took 20 shots. 12 were threes. They made 2.
say: In the third, the Spurs took twenty shots. Twelve were threes. They made two.

text: This time, Chuck had a point. Miss after miss off the rim, the Knicks grabbing the rebounds and running. The Spurs lost the quarter 26 to 14, and the lead was down to 15.
say: This time, Chuck had a point. Miss after miss off the rim, the Knicks grabbing the rebounds and running. The Spurs lost the quarter twenty-six to fourteen, and the lead was down to fifteen.

text: Now, you'd say, if the threes won't fall, take it inside. And in the fourth, that's exactly what the Spurs did.
19 shots in the fourth. Only 5 threes, and 7 at the rim. And the result? 4 for 19. Just as bad as the third.
say: Nineteen shots in the fourth. Only five threes, and seven at the rim. And the result? Four for nineteen. Just as bad as the third.

text: The problem was on the other end.
Look at how close the defender's hand was to the ball on every Spurs shot.

In the fourth, it averaged just 2.7 feet. Almost every shot had a hand right in front of it, the tightest the Spurs were guarded all night. Of their 19 shots, only one came with the nearest hand more than six feet away.
say: In the fourth, it averaged just two point seven feet. Almost every shot had a hand right in front of it, the tightest the Spurs were guarded all night. Of their nineteen shots, only one came with the nearest hand more than six feet away.

text: Knicks coach Mike Brown said they didn't change the game plan.
Spurs coach Mitch Johnson didn't make excuses.
Pressure on the rim, rolls to the basket, running the floor. In the second half, all of it disappeared, and the whole team was pushed back on its heels.
With nine and a half minutes left in the fourth, the Spurs were still up 20. Five minutes later, it was down to 4.
say: With nine and a half minutes left in the fourth, the Spurs were still up twenty. Five minutes later, it was down to four.

text: In those five minutes, the Knicks went 20 to 4, and all 4 Spurs points were Castle free throws. Not one field goal.
say: In those five minutes, the Knicks went twenty to four, and all four Spurs points were Castle free throws. Not one field goal.

text: OK. Now we can go back to the thing that didn't add up.
say: Okay. Now we can go back to the thing that didn't add up.

text: By shot difficulty, the Spurs' second-half looks were worth about 39 points, right in line with the first half. They scored 19. That's 20 short.
say: By shot difficulty, the Spurs' second-half looks were worth about thirty-nine points, right in line with the first half. They scored nineteen. That's twenty short.

text: Those 21 bonus points from the first half? They gave almost all of them right back. And the Knicks, in the fourth, made about 7 more than expected.
say: Those twenty-one bonus points from the first half? They gave almost all of them right back. And the Knicks, in the fourth, made about seven more than expected.

text: So most of that 29 was borrowed to begin with. The Spurs paid it back after halftime, and the Knicks squeezed out the rest.
say: So most of that twenty-nine was borrowed to begin with. The Spurs paid it back after halftime, and the Knicks squeezed out the rest.

text: But remember, with three and a half minutes to go, the Spurs still had a 7-point lead. How do you lose that?
say: But remember, with three and a half minutes to go, the Spurs still had a seven-point lead. How do you lose that?

text: So let's go through those last three and a half minutes, one possession at a time.
3:31 left. Wembanyama hits a jumper. Spurs up 104 to 97, a 7-point lead.
say: Three thirty-one left. Wembanyama hits a jumper. Spurs up one-oh-four to ninety-seven, a seven-point lead.

text: Believe it or not, that was the Spurs' last field goal of the night.
Alvarado answers with a three, 104 to 100. Fox misses a three at the other end, and the ball is back in Brunson's hands.
say: Alvarado answers with a three, one-oh-four to one hundred. Fox misses a three at the other end, and the ball is back in Brunson's hands.

text: Two and a half minutes left. The Knicks run a pick-and-roll and get Wembanyama switched onto Brunson.
Alvarado drives, kicks it back out to Brunson, and the Spurs never switch back.
This time Wemby is right on him, hand up, less than three feet from the ball.
Brunson doesn't care. Twenty-seven feet. Up it goes.
And it's good. 104 to 103.
say: And it's good. One-oh-four to one-oh-three.

text: Next trip, Hart picks off a Fox pass. Luckily, Hart can't finish the layup on the break, and Fox gets the rebound back.
1:47 left, Wembanyama is fouled and goes to the line. Misses them both.
say: One forty-seven left, Wembanyama is fouled and goes to the line. Misses them both.

text: Asked about those free throws, Wemby kept it simple.
Then Brunson goes at Castle. Floater, good. Knicks lead 105 to 104, their first lead of the night.
say: Then Brunson goes at Castle. Floater, good. Knicks lead one-oh-five to one-oh-four, their first lead of the night.

text: Castle steps out of bounds, another turnover. Luckily, the Knicks come up empty, and the shot clock runs out.
30 seconds left, Fox misses a jumper. Castle grabs the offensive board and gets fouled by Hart. Two free throws, both good. Spurs back in front, 106 to 105.
say: Thirty seconds left, Fox misses a jumper. Castle grabs the offensive board and gets fouled by Hart. Two free throws, both good. Spurs back in front, one-oh-six to one-oh-five.

text: Knicks timeout. Brunson drives, floater, no good. The ball bounces way out, and Fox chases it down in the frontcourt.
Let's freeze it right here.
Spurs up one. 13 seconds left. Their ball. And the shot clock reads 24, more than the time left in the game. A shot-clock violation can't even happen.
say: Spurs up one. Thirteen seconds left. Their ball. And the shot clock reads twenty-four, more than the time left in the game. A shot-clock violation can't even happen.

text: So how do you play this?

Simple. Do nothing. Just hold the ball. The Knicks have to foul and send you to the line. Make both, and you're up three. The best they can do is a three to tie. Anyone who's ever played the game knows that.
But Fox grabs it, never stops, and goes straight at the rim.
Here comes Anunoby, from behind.
Pinned on the glass!
Asked about that play afterward, Mike Brown gave Fox the benefit of the doubt.
But look at the clock. Fox has the ball with 13 seconds left. He leaves his feet at 12.5. Less than a second. Does that look like a guy trying to kill the clock?
say: But look at the clock. Fox has the ball with thirteen seconds left. He leaves his feet at twelve point five. Less than a second. Does that look like a guy trying to kill the clock?

text: Wembanyama was on the floor when it happened.
That one play handed the Knicks a free possession. And in the end, that's the possession that beat them.
Alvarado comes up with the loose ball, and the Spurs foul with 5.7 seconds left. Only their second foul of the quarter, so no free throws. The Knicks call timeout and advance it to the frontcourt.
say: Alvarado comes up with the loose ball, and the Spurs foul with five point seven seconds left. Only their second foul of the quarter, so no free throws. The Knicks call timeout and advance it to the frontcourt.

text: Anunoby takes it out.
Once Brunson has it, Anunoby just parks outside the arc, like he's got nothing to do with this play.
Brunson lets it fly from 31 feet. No good.
say: Brunson lets it fly from thirty-one feet. No good.

text: But the moment it's up, Anunoby crashes in from beyond the arc. Wembanyama and Fox were both pulled out by Brunson, and the other three Spurs are stuck on their own men. Nobody touches him.
Tipped in!
Mike Brown said he'd challenged Anunoby by name before the game.
Anunoby had one offensive rebound all game. That was it.
The Spurs had 1.2 seconds left. Towns tipped away the inbound. Game over.
say: The Spurs had one point two seconds left. Towns tipped away the inbound. Game over.

text: The Knicks led this game for a grand total of 53.8 seconds.
say: The Knicks led this game for a grand total of fifty-three point eight seconds.

text: So, back to the question we started with. How did the Spurs lose this game?

In the first half, that 29-point lead was mostly hot shooting. In the second half, the shooting went cold. In the third, the threes kept clanking. In the fourth, the Knicks' defense squeezed them bit by bit. But all of that only cost them the lead.
say: In the first half, that twenty-nine-point lead was mostly hot shooting. In the second half, the shooting went cold. In the third, the threes kept clanking. In the fourth, the Knicks' defense squeezed them bit by bit. But all of that only cost them the lead.

text: What really gave the game away were the possessions the Spurs threw away in the final three and a half minutes. Above all, that Fox layup, a shot he never needed to take.
Wembanyama, after the game.
Three days later, back in San Antonio, the Spurs lost Game 5, 94 to 90. And the Knicks won their first championship since 1973.
say: Three days later, back in San Antonio, the Spurs lost Game five, ninety-four to ninety. And the Knicks won their first championship since nineteen seventy-three.
